**DMPG-retningslinjen: Udredning af ADHD hos børn og unge i hospitalsregi og speciallægepraksis** (The DMPG Guideline: Assessment of ADHD in children and adolescents in hospital settings and specialist practices) is a clinical guideline document published in early 2025 [^src1]. It serves as a newly established, management-supported framework that directly influences the prioritization of assessment elements within the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] [^src1]. The guideline is recognized as a critical factor for driving improvements in registration practices and the fulfillment of national quality indicators [^src1].

Within the broader context of Denmark's national ADHD strategy and the annual evaluation of psychiatric facilities, the integration of the DMPG guidelines into quality measurement represents a significant strategic shift. Specifically, the guideline has directly shaped the formulation of new quality metrics. For instance, [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] leans heavily on the DMPG guideline's recommendations, particularly regarding the requirement to gather information about a child's or adolescent's daily life in institutional or school settings [^src2]. By securing management backing, the guideline has successfully elevated the priority of these recommended assessment elements across both public and private treatment actors [^src1].
